summary_of_core_decisions: The paper argues that Leibniz's Laws are not too rigid if properties are indexed to times and worlds. It demonstrates this by solving the problem of identity over time (Bobby) and identity across worlds (Chisholm's Adam/Noah), and addresses the epistemic challenge of identifying transworld objects by appealing to world-indexed properties and Kripke's descriptive account of possible worlds.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Defends a specific solution (property-indexing) to a family of problems
